I got dressed and headed outside.

sentences.sentence: it was obvious why she was enraged.
`` Yes, yes!
But we've reached the end of our patience!''
She had a knife, God noticed.
Shiva roared, her husband and obvious backup.
He was wielding a staff studded with blades, and when God saw his eyes, he felt a tingle on the back of his neck, like one of his hair follicles was about to grow a second head.
God stepped back onto the threshold and closed the door.
The gods pressed their hands against it and pushed against it with every ounce of their supernatural strength, and God could feel the door vibrate in its hinges.
`` I'm sorry to have offended you,'' God called through the wood.
`` I was only trying to help.''
The gods quieted and turned as a whole to face him.
He could see them thinking their way through their options.
The door, he was sure, would not take a hit from any of them, but it had its limits.
Their rage and desperation seemed to have pushed the goddesses to a new level of fury, and he couldn't help but admire that.
Shiva shook her head and turned back to the door.
God winced and then relaxed a bit when he heard her speak.
It was as though she'd calmed herself in the past minute, and his ears couldn't believe it.
`` We will come back for you when we are ready,'' Shiva said.
The other goddesses grumbled, but she ignored them, and the three of them left as one.
God unlocked the door and waited for them to leave before he let himself out to watch them go.
Their shoulders seemed to slump as they crossed into the dark, and he wondered what he'd done to earn their mercy.
Was it a trick?
Was it a lie?

sentences.sentence: magazines, same bland walls.
There were even some children in their parents' arms, some adults sitting on their own, a few talking quietly on their cell phones.
The only difference I could see was that a huge woman with a clipboard was in charge of everyone in the room.
There were no desks, no sign in sheet.
I mean, sure, there could be a small computer monitor tucked behind the chair or something, but no.
Nothing.
Just her clipboard, a pen tucked in the top corner, and a bunch of names and phone numbers on one half.
She was scribbling down some random notes with the other.
As soon as I got through the door, she stopped and looked at me.
I swear I felt a chill go through my body when she looked at me.
*We need to talk,* she said with no preamble.
She didn't sound like the person I had just spoken to on my car speaker phone.
*Take a seat.
She pointed to the chair beside her, so I sat down.
She looked at me with the expression of someone who has been watching me for a very long time.
She opened her mouth to speak, but the phone in her pocket suddenly rang.
*"Doctor's Office,"* she said into it.
Her voice was flat, devoid of inflection.
*You're on hold, we'll take your call after your next turn.
* She hung up the phone and looked at me again.
*It's never going to end.
*"Doctor's office?
"* I said.
*Am I in a dental office?
She looked at me blankly.
*What?
I had to think about that one for a second.
*Is this where my dentist's office takes place?
*Why would you say that?
I didn't really have an answer.
I just had the feeling.
*Well, why are you here?
*I'm a dental technician.

sentences.sentence: Shadow, better than the Fonz.
'If you got the package, and you're wondering what it is, read this: Tony has made you a present for your eighteenth birthday.
It's a present to remind you that you're not alone, that he's always with you and always will be.'
The note fell onto the floor, and a lump formed in my throat.
I wiped my eyes with the back of my sleeve.
I turned the package over in my hands.
It was a thin, square box made of some kind of dull silver material.
I opened the top of it, and found the inside was lined with what looked like a million tiny plastic mirrors.
I was about to throw it across the room when I saw a thin strip of dark blue ribbon attached to a tiny tag.
Written on the tag were the words `` For the birthday boy!
It didn't take me long to realize what was on the ribbon - a pair of Tony's shoelaces.
They were in mint condition, and looked pretty damn good on the mirror-lined box.
I sat down on my bed.
`` I'll just put them on the shelf,'' I told myself, my hands trembling.
They were so much like Tony's, and so pretty.
They were all I had left of my brother.
I slipped the laces through my shoes.
They were a little bit too long, but that only made them look a little bit prettier.
I slipped my foot into my favourite pair of Tony's shoes.

sentences.sentence: a tightrope with a strong wind blowing at me, no matter the weather, no matter how calm it is.
And when I land, I feel like I could jump higher, or longer, or further.
But I have to remember, as the man in the lab coat says, that this is an illusion.
I don't know exactly how long I've been doing this.
For as long as I can remember I've done this, though I've never understood why.
I think I was even born like this, but my parents and everyone who raises me don't understand what it is.

I've been brought into many different medical facilities for this, and I've seen many doctors in white coats, who do this thing with me, where they do all kinds of tests, in a very repetitive way, for hours on end.
I often feel like a bug under their microscope, or a mouse in a cage they observe for research purposes.
Every day, I would jump the way a lab animal jumps on a wheel.
Sometimes the people in white coats do tests on me to see if I'm "abnormal" or different, or if something is wrong, but I really don't know how to explain the feeling.
It's like a feeling of freedom, or freedom from something or someone.
It is a very liberating feeling, one I often associate with jumping into the air.
But like the man in the lab coat would say, it's an illusion.
But now that I think about it, I've never been told why I do this.
Why have I been told about it being an illusion?
And what is the reason I have this ability?
And what is the reason I have to do this?
I never felt like I had a choice.
I've come here to see the man in the white coat many times, but I'm getting a bit tired of it now.
I never see any of the other tests they do.

I've been brought into many different medical facilities for this, and I've seen many doctors in white coats, who do this thing with me, where they do all kinds of tests, in a very repetitive way, for hours on end. I often feel like a bug under their microscope, or a mouse in a cage they observe for research purposes. 

 

Every day, I would jump the way a lab animal jumps on a wheel. Sometimes the people in white coats do tests on me to see if I'm "abnormal" or different, or if something is wrong, but I really don't know how to explain the feeling. It's like a feeling of freedom, or freedom from something or someone. It is a very liberating feeling, one I often associate with jumping into the air. But like the man in the lab coat would say, it's an illusion. 

 

But now that I think about it, I've never been told why I do this. Why have I been told about it being an illusion? And what is the reason I have this ability? And what is the reason I have to do this? I never felt like I had a choice. 

 

I've come here to see the man in the white coat many times, but I'm getting a bit tired of it now. I never see any of the other tests they do.

He came in complaining of back pain, so I ordered some tests to get started.
I listened to his lungs and heart, and then to the rest of his upper chest and back.
Nothing seemed wrong to me; no wheezing or crackles in his lungs, his heart sounded fine, and no popping noises or grating from his chest or back.
It was during the abdominal exam that I knew he was in trouble.
It started as I palpated his stomach.
He winced and groaned a little, and I thought it was just nerves.
He tensed up and grunted, I thought he was just apprehensive.
Then I felt the movement inside his abdomen.
It felt like something inside of him was walking around.
My patient screamed and I took a step back, thinking that was what I was feeling, and not something he had inside him.
I checked my latex gloves, they hadn't broken, so I figured my patient was just trying to be funny.
I looked back over at him and saw he'd lost the fight.
His skin was so pale you could read your newspaper through him.
His eyes had rolled up into his head and his back arched in a grotesque shape.
I was about to call for the nurses to come assist me when I felt the thing inside his belly.
The skin felt like it was being tugged at, but I couldn't see anything happening.
It felt like the thing inside him was walking around inside him.
I didn't realize I was crying until I touched a tear that ran down the side of my nose.
I went back to the patient's chart and checked to see what I'd missed, but the history was pretty clear.
I heard footsteps in the hallway outside the exam room and looked up.
